name: Yellowstone Lamar Valley Wolves
dates: Year round; best Dec–Mar and Jun
unique: The best place on earth to watch wild wolves hunt in a broad glacial valley, alongside bison herds, pronghorn and the occasional grizzly.
buzz: Dawn in winter is the consensus best; bring a spotting scope and patience. Wolf watchers share sightings generously.

name: Grand Teton and Jenny Lake
unique: A twelve-peak granite skyline rising straight out of a lake, with a boat shuttle to hidden falls and a canyon that rewards an early start.
buzz: The Teton crest is the most photographed range in the country and it earns it; parking at Jenny Lake fills by 8am.

name: Wind River Range Backpack
unique: The most remote alpine range in the lower 48, with Gannett Peak, hundreds of glacial lakes and a Cirque of the Towers that climbers dream about.
buzz: Backpackers call it the best wilderness in America and warn about mosquitoes, river crossings and sudden storms. Carry a bear canister.

name: Jackson Hole Corbet's Couloir
unique: A 3,000-vertical-foot resort with a legendary couloir you have to jump into from the cornice, and a tram that gets you there in nine minutes.
buzz: Experts call it the most challenging in-bounds terrain in America; everyone else watches from the tram. Snow is deep and the tram line is real.

name: Devils Tower
unique: A 867-foot columnar basalt butte that looks engineered, sacred to Plains tribes and still climbable on traditional routes.
buzz: The walk around the base is easy and awe inspiring; climbers need a permit and June closures respect tribal ceremonies.

name: Cheyenne Frontier Days
unique: The world's largest outdoor rodeo, ten days of bull riding, pancake breakfasts, a carnival and country concerts in a town that empties into the stands.
buzz: The rodeo is top-tier and the pancake breakfast is a civic ritual; book lodging in January. Heat and crowds are real.

name: Fossil Butte National Monument
unique: A butte of ancient lakebed where 50 million year old fish are quarried out whole, with a visitor center of prepared specimens and a quarry trail you can hike.
buzz: The fish fossils are astounding and the quarry trail is short; the park is remote and the preparation lab is where people linger.

name: Bighorn Canyon
unique: A canyon 1,000 feet deep where the Bighorn River runs between Wyoming and Montana, with wild horses on the uplands and a lake for fishing and boating.
buzz: The drive along the rim and the boat up the canyon are the two ways to see it; the park is quiet and the wild horses are a bonus.

name: Fort Laramie
customer: History families, trail people, school groups
unique: The fur trading post and army fort that anchored the Oregon Trail, with 20 original buildings, Officers' Row and the treaty grounds where the 1851 council was held.
buzz: The ranger tours and the restored barracks are the visit; it is free and the scale is bigger than people expect on the high plains.

name: Hot Springs State Park
unique: A free state bathhouse with water at 104 degrees, a travertine terrace above the Bighorn River and a buffalo herd in the park.
buzz: The free bathhouse is the local institution and the state park is free; the commercial pools next door have slides and quieter hours.

name: Cloud Peak Wilderness
unique: A quarter million acres of roadless Bighorn high country with 13,000 foot peaks, glacial lakes and cutthroat trout, reached by trails from West Tensleep.
buzz: Backpackers say it is the emptiest big wilderness in the lower 48 and the weather turns fast; the trails are unmarked in places.

name: Cody Nite Rodeo
unique: A nightly amateur rodeo in the town Buffalo Bill built, with broncs, bull riding and a crowd that knows the difference between a good ride and a lucky one.
buzz: It is unpolished and genuine; kids love the mutton busting. Pair with the Buffalo Bill Center of the West.

name: Medicine Wheel
unique: A 80 foot stone wheel at 9,600 feet on the Bighorn range, aligned with the summer solstice and considered sacred by several tribes, reached by a 1.5 mile walk.
buzz: The walk is the pilgrimage and the wheel is roped off for protection; visitors are asked to treat it as a church and the altitude is serious.

name: Sinks Canyon
unique: A river that disappears into a limestone cave and reappears a quarter mile down the canyon, with a viewing bridge and trout you can feed at the rise.
buzz: The disappearing river is the story and the trout at the rise are a hit with children; the canyon trails climb above the road.

name: Flaming Gorge
company: National Park Service and Bureau of Reclamation
unique: A red rock canyon flooded into a 91 mile reservoir with trophy lake trout and a dam you can tour, on the Green River above the Colorado.
buzz: Anglers come for the big lake trout and the canyon drive on the Sheep Creek loop is the scenery; the water is cold and the wind is strong.

name: National Historic Trails Interpretive Center
customer: History families, road trippers, school groups
unique: A free center where the Oregon, California, Mormon and Pony Express trails all crossed the North Platte, with covered wagons you can climb into and a simulated river crossing.
buzz: The wagon and the crossing simulation are what children remember; the diaries and the maps are the adult version and the view of Casper Mountain is the setting.

name: South Pass City
customer: History families, ghost town hunters, road trippers
unique: A gold camp of 30 original buildings at the crossing of the Oregon Trail, where Wyoming gave women the vote in 1869 and the first woman justice of the peace was elected.
buzz: The restored buildings and the Esther Hobart Morris story are the history; the drive over South Pass is half the visit.

name: Ten Sleep Canyon
unique: A limestone canyon with hundreds of sport climbing routes on both walls, and a road that switchbacks 2,000 feet up to the Bighorn plateau.
buzz: Climbers call it one of the best limestone destinations in the country and the drive is the scenic route; the canyon is hot in summer and the rock is sharp.

name: Wyoming Dinosaur Center
unique: A museum with a 106 foot Supersaurus and a dig site on a nearby mesa where visitors can join a real excavation for a day.
buzz: The dig program is the reason people come from other states and the mounted skeletons are the rainy day version; book the dig weeks ahead.

name: Wyoming Territorial Prison
customer: History people, families, true crime fans
unique: A stone territorial prison where Butch Cassidy served time, with cell blocks, a broom factory and a warden's house, on a bluff above Laramie.
buzz: The cell block and the stories of the inmates are the tour; it is small and the self guided map lets you move at your own pace.

name: Fort Bridger
customer: History families, trail people, school groups
unique: A fur trading post turned army fort on the Oregon Trail, with original stone buildings, a museum and a Labor Day rendezvous with mountain men and buckskinners.
buzz: The rendezvous weekend is the time to go and the stone buildings are the real thing; the site is quiet otherwise and the grounds are free to walk.

name: Guernsey State Park
unique: A reservoir with CCC built stone picnic shelters and a castle-like museum, and the Register Cliff where emigrants carved their names on the Oregon Trail.
buzz: The CCC stonework is the reason architecture people stop and the lake is the summer swim; Register Cliff is a short drive away.

name: Independence Rock
unique: A granite dome the emigrants called the Register of the Desert, covered in carved names, where wagon trains aimed to arrive by July 4 to make the mountains before snow.
buzz: The names on the rock are the thing and the climb is short; it is a good leg stretch on Highway 220 and the ruts are nearby.

name: King's Saddlery
unique: A saddlery and rope shop with a museum of braided rawhide and horsehair hitches behind the sales floor, run by a family that still makes tack for working ranches.
buzz: The museum cases are free and the workmanship is museum grade; the shop sells ropes and hats and the staff will explain what you are looking at.

name: Wyoming Frontier Prison
unique: A preserved territorial prison with a death row cell block, a gas chamber and graffiti carved by inmates, toured by guides who do not soften the details.
buzz: The tour is grim and fascinating; guides tell the stories of specific prisoners. Not for young children.

name: Intermittent Spring
unique: A spring that flows heavily for several minutes and then stops, probably because of a natural siphon in the mountain, reached by a mile and a half trail.
buzz: The timing is unpredictable and that is the fun; scientists have studied it and locals take visitors up in summer.

name: Jim Gatchell Memorial Museum
unique: A drugstore owner's collection of frontier weapons, saddles and Lakota artifacts, with a room on the Johnson County War and the cattle barons' invasion.
buzz: The Johnson County War exhibit is the reason history people stop and the collection is bigger than the building suggests; it takes 90 minutes.

name: Fort Caspar
unique: A reconstructed 1860s military post and emigrant crossing on the Oregon Trail, with a ferry replica and a museum of the telegraph line.
buzz: The rebuilt buildings and the wagon ruts are the visit and the summer demonstrations bring it alive; it is small and the river setting is pleasant.

name: Trail End State Historic Site
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 1913 Flemish revival mansion built by a cattle baron and later a governor, with original furniture and a view over Sheridan.
buzz: The house is unrestored in the best way and the guides know the family; the tour runs on the hour and is short.

name: University of Wyoming Geological Museum
unique: A free museum with a Apatosaurus skeleton, a wall of Wyoming fossils and a mastodon, in a university building that has been collecting since the 1880s.
buzz: The dinosaur hall is the family stop and the fossil collection is serious; it is free and takes an hour.

name: White Mountain Petroglyphs
customer: Rock art people, road trippers, photographers
unique: A sandstone cliff covered with petroglyphs of bison, elk and human figures, some a thousand years old, reached by a short walk on a dirt road.
buzz: The figures are large and clear and the site is unguarded; the drive is 15 miles of gravel and the wind never stops.

name: Bear River State Park
unique: A small state park with a herd of bison and elk you can see from the road, and a river walk, on the edge of Evanston.
buzz: The bison are the reason to stop and the park is free; it is a good break on Interstate 80 with children.

name: Campbell County Rockpile Museum
customer: Local history people, energy workers, families
unique: A museum of the coal and oil boom that built Gillette, with a coal camp kitchen, a rail car and a room on the homesteaders who came before.
buzz: The energy history is unusually honest about the booms and busts; it is free and the staff are local.

name: Riverton Museum
unique: A small museum on the Wind River with Arapaho and Shoshone beadwork, a pioneer kitchen and a room on the oil boom that changed the town.
buzz: The Native collection and the local stories are the reason to stop; it is volunteer run and the staff will talk.

name: Washakie Museum
unique: A museum on the Bighorn Basin with a mammoth skeleton found nearby, Native beadwork and a room on the German POW camp that was here in the war.
buzz: The mammoth and the POW story are the surprises; it is small and the staff are proud of the local finds.

name: Wyoming Pioneer Memorial Museum
unique: A museum on the state fairgrounds with a pioneer cabin, a one room school and the saddles and brands of the ranches that settled the Platte valley.
buzz: The buildings out back are the charm and it is free; the state fair in August fills the grounds.
